preconditions.description: The number of towns in Udayland is between 2 and 2 * 10^5.
Each road goes from town i to some other town a_i, where 1 <= a_i <= n and a_i != i.

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer.

postconditions.expression: output represents the number of ways to flip some set of roads so that the resulting network is not confusing
postconditions.description: The output represents the number of valid configurations of flipping roads to avoid forming a confusing network.

invariants.expression: n is the number of towns
invariants.description: The number of towns n is a fixed value given as input.

invariants.expression: a_i is the destination of the road from town i
invariants.description: Each a_i indicates the town a road goes to from town i.

invariants.expression: flipping a road means changing its direction
invariants.description: Flipping a road means reversing its direction.

invariants.expression: a network is confusing if it forms a directed cycle
invariants.description: A network is considered confusing if there exists a sequence of roads forming a directed cycle.
